## Body

PASS-WITH-NOTES at 44e4974613311537047b346be285f5ec733507cd, round 1.

#316 N1-N3 and security new-1/new-2 are closed:
- N1: the API documentation now states FIFO eviction at 256, regardless of
  binding state; memory only, not hydrated at boot. The spine's settlement
  facts guard boot recovery, while a resend reads its row. No durable replay
  cache is implied.
- N2: pane observation selects stop first, including a dropped sender, before
  a ready tick. The 32-round control passes; the unbiased mutant fails at round0.
  An already-running observation is still joined, not interrupted.
- N3 / new-2: SpawnHold owns the launch mutex and clears its diagnostic name
  in Drop before its OwnedMutexGuard releases. Both spawn and revive use it,
  and revive names its own checks before handing that same hold to the owned
  launch task. Early return, next-holder acquisition and panic unwinding all
  leave no stale name. No public raw spawn-lock/name-setting bypass remains;
  stop's private mutex acquisition is a join, not a spawn path.
- New-1: SpawnHold::name rejects every control character and recognized line
  separator through render::is_one_line; spawn names its folder only after
  printable_path. Newline/ESC controls pass; removing the guard fails.

Shutdown ordering / ownership:
All twelve concurrent phase tasks are awaited by join!, not try_join!, before
delivery/event flush and physical store close. Only after those joins/cleanup
does shutdown propagate errors. Moving the concurrent work into tasks does not
remove the sequential barriers: SpawnWaits::stop remains first and bounded;
HTTP/governance are signalled; park notices and lapse follower are aborted/joined;
all phase tasks join; admitted work flushes; stores close.
The practical F242 ordering passed on this exact source: the private tmux
control client left while a real HTTP event stream still held the drain, then
shutdown completed and the private server's other session survived.

There was not, and is not, a universal finish-order constraint between tmux
release and an empty/short HTTP drain. Release is started before the concurrent
join, independently of drain. A deterministic blocked-release fixture showed
HTTP may finish first, while the group still waits for release before returning.
The former code had the same pre-started release and concurrent join. This is a
qualification of the ordering claim, not a regression introduced by this PR.

A phase future that panics returns an error naming that phase, while the other
phase still joins; the independent panic/control fixture passed. The caller's
normal shutdown path waits for every phase, so no added phase task is detached
after a returned shutdown result. As before, the tmux release's inner teardown
failure is intentionally tolerated; that is not the generic phase-panic path.
There is no new global timeout for a wedged phase; the change diagnoses it.

Notes owed:
1. Cancellation is a different ownership path. Dropping the future returned
   by spawn_phase drops its JoinHandle and detaches the already-started task.
   A latch probe dropped the join wait, then released work and observed it finish.
   Likewise cancelling the outer shutdown during join! does not abort/join the
   newly spawned phase tasks. The production CLI awaits shutdown directly, so
   no normal-use regression was demonstrated. Document this cancellation scope
   or add cancellation-safe ownership if a caller needs it; do not claim that
   every cancellation leaves zero running phase tasks.
2. HTTP/control timers still measure the wrapper's wait when their work already
   began before timed(): HTTP shutdown is signalled and control release's blocking
   task is spawned earlier. The independent end logs fix the shared-task starvation
   problem, but are not complete signal-to-release durations in every phase.
   Avoid presenting them as such.

The merge preserves the phase/hold/stop fixes and main's port changes; diff-check
passes. Federation fan-in's unchanged unbiased selectors and detach_all's
blocking calls remain the explicitly named deferrals, not fixes claimed here.

Cost:
Twelve one-shot Tokio tasks per stop, global per daemon, not per seat; no added
steady-state process launch, poll or timer. The existing single observer loop's
default600ms interval and per-live-pane pass shape are unchanged; bias can only
spare an extra pass at stop. A normal spawn makes two name writes plus Drop's
clear; a successful revive can make three name writes plus clear. These are
O(1) request-time mutex operations, not a periodic cost. Existing blocking tmux
detach work is unchanged. No live-fleet bounce or before/after cost claim.
